sections.title: Habit and cultivation
sections.text: Lemongrass is an aromatic perennial grass cultivated in tropical regions. It forms a clump about 0.9–1.8 m tall and 0.9–1.2 m wide. Its leaves are long and narrow, and the bases of its stems are thickened.

sections.title: Leaves and culinary use
sections.text: The leaves and tender stem bases are used as a flavouring. The plate shows the clump, a leaf detail and a spikelet. Flowering is uncommon in cultivation in some regions and is not needed for culinary identification.
